channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: China Set to Lead World in Energy Investment in 2026, CCTV Says
item.description: China is expected to invest $940 billion in energy in 2026, the most by any country, according to the Global Energy Transition Report 2026 released by the China Enterprise Reform and Development Society, China Central Television reported Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: China Raises Delegate Count to 2,360 for 2027 Party Congress
item.description: China set a quota of 2,360 delegates for the Communist Party’s 21st national congress in 2027, 60 more than for the previous gathering, Xinhua News Agency reported Sunday, citing the party’s Organization Department.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: AI Slump Revives Asia’s Forgotten Trades From China to India
item.description: The unraveling of the AI trade after the US midterm elections is forcing investors to rethink their Asia playbook, reviving demand for out-of-favor Chinese and Indian stocks as well as companies poised to benefit from easing inflation and trade tensions.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Vishnoi and Winnie Hsu

item.title: Australia Home Sales Rise in Fledgling Sign of Property Recovery
item.description: Australian home sales and auction clearance rates climbed, offering hopes of a recovery for a property market that has slumped as interest rates rose this year.
item.dc:creator: Richard Henderson

item.title: Meta’s $25 Billion Bond Sale Highlights Shifting Landscape for Tech Debt
item.description: Selling billions of dollars of corporate bonds on Election Day seemed like a real gamble.
item.dc:creator: Davide Barbuscia

item.title: New Chief of Staff, Chain Reaction Tech Selloff
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Yorkville Ives & Co. Partner & Senior Managing Director Dan Ives, Rutgers-Eagleton Center for Public Interest Polling Director Ashley Koning, PNC Asset Management Group Chief Investment Officer Amanda Agati, Travel Journalist Brittany Chang, Atlanta Journal-Constitution Washington Bureau Chief Tia Mitchell, General Catalyst Chairman & Managing Director Ken Chenault and Composer & Pianist Missy Mazzoli. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ken Chenault on Leadership in an Age of AI
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, General Catalyst Chairman and Managing Director and former American Express CEO Ken Chenault discusses leadership, diversity and responsible AI, arguing that executives need the courage to stand by their values even as political and technological pressures intensify. Chenault tells host David Gura that companies should pursue innovation while protecting safety, broadening opportunity and ensuring AI ultimately improves people's lives. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: A Historic First for Women at the Metropolitan Opera
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, composer Missy Mazzoli discusses adapting George Saunders's Lincoln in the Bardo and becoming the first woman composer to have a world premiere at the Metropolitan Opera. Mazzoli tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini how punk helped shape her musical sensibility and why her long collaboration with librettist Royce Vavrek was essential to transforming Saunders's sprawling ghost story into an opera. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How the Iran War Is Making Alaskans Both Richer and Poorer
item.description: Oil prices have surged across the United States as a result of the ongoing war in Iran. This means higher costs for households in most states, but in Alaska, the state government is bringing in new revenue from its high oil production to offset those higher costs. Some of the revenue is then redistributed to Alaskans through the state’s unique sovereign wealth fund. While most Americans disapprove of the war in Iran, Alaska may emerge as a quiet winner from one of the conflict’s most painful economic side effects: higher oil prices. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Protein Craze Fuels an Investment Boom in Livestock Health
item.description: Animal health companies are tapping into the protein craze, investing billions of dollars to build up businesses focused on making cattle, pigs and poultry healthier for human consumption.
item.dc:creator: Ilena Peng

item.title: Young Travelers Are Warming Up to Cruises
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News travel journalist Brittany Chang explains why cruises are attracting more Gen Z and millennial travelers as higher airfare and hotel costs make all-inclusive vacations increasingly appealing. Chang tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that cruise lines are courting younger passengers with mega ships, entertainment, adult-only spaces and nostalgia, with some sailings costing as little as about $30 a day. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Economy and Democracy Drove the Blue Wave
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Rutgers University's Ashley Koning says affordability, concerns about democracy and government corruption helped drive voters toward Democrats, with significant shifts among Latino, young and independent voters. Koning tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Democrats now face pressure to deliver tangible results on affordability before the 2028 election cycle. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Berkshire Makes Record $9.6 Billion Buyback
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Insurance Analyst Matthew Palazola breaks down Berkshire Hathaway's third-quarter results, including a record $9.6 billion in share buybacks and weaker insurance earnings. Palazola tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that CEO Greg Abel is putting Berkshire's massive cash reserves to work through buybacks, acquisitions and equity investments while maintaining the measured approach associated with Warren Buffett. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Top Turkish Regulators Taken Into Custody in Fund Probe
item.description: Turkish authorities detained top officials from the country’s regulators on Saturday, local media reported, the latest executives to be caught up in a widening fund scandal.
item.dc:creator: Murat Oztaskin

item.title: Wall Street Strategists Call Stock Rout a Fresh Reason to Buy
item.description: A slew of Wall Street strategists were banking on a short-term selloff following the US midterm elections to give investors an opportunity to buy stocks at a discount.
item.dc:creator: Emily Forgash

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: The guide for when to pee during movies, taking PTO to play GTA, ignoring the Foie Gras ban, and kids loving their mom and dad's music: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Jobs Surge Raises Odds of December Fed Hike
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics Chief US Economist Anna Wong says October's surprisingly strong jobs report showed hiring broadening into white collar, manufacturing and transportation jobs, strengthening the case for another Federal Reserve rate hike. Wong tells hosts Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo how the Bloomberg Price Project uses millions of alternative data points to provide an independent, more granular measure of US inflation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway Boosts Buybacks as Operating Income Slips
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. spent about $9.6 billion to buy back its own shares in the third quarter, a sign the company’s executives viewed the stock as undervalued. But declining insurance underwriting weighed on its operating earnings in a mixed quarter for the company.
item.dc:creator: Alex Rajbhandari

item.title: Crypto’s Trump-Fueled Washington Boom Reaches Its Endgame
item.description: Crypto’s extraordinary run of political good fortune in Washington has come to an abrupt halt. With Democrats set to control Congress following their midterm sweep, the industry faces the prospect of tougher rules and closer scrutiny of its ties to President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Teresa Xie and Scott Patterson
